title: Adaptive alert dampening, regional circuit interlock, and automated responder playbooks
creator: Anita Patel
description: Reduce noisy pages and prevent cascading multi-region failovers by implementing an SLO-aware adaptive alert dampening layer, a regional circuit interlock to coordinate failover decisions, and automated on-call responder playbooks that can execute safe mitigations. This ticket covers design, prototype, testing in staging, and a canary rollout path for the new alerting stack. The goal is to reduce actionable pager noise by ~60% for low-impact SLO degradations while preserving fast escalation for high-severity, high-customer-impact incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Alert dampener evaluates alerts against SLO burn rate and active mitigation state and suppresses low-impact alerts automatically; suppression must be auditable and reversible.
Regional circuit interlock prevents automatic cross-region failover unless region health and capacity signals indicate safe evacuation; documented policy available in Console.
Runbook playbooks can be triggered automatically and manually; automated steps must include a dry-run mode and an opt-out toggle for on-call.
End-to-end tests (chaos + synthetic) demonstrate at least 60% reduction in page volume for non-critical SLO noise without increasing user-visible error rate by more than 2%.
Telemetry: dashboards show suppressed alert counts, reasons, SLO burn rate correlation, and time-to-resolution for incidents where suppressions occurred.
Canary rollout across 10% of production traffic with rollback criteria defined (increase in P99 latency > 10% or unhandled escalation misses > 1 per week per service).
notes: Motivation: We currently over-page for transient SLO blips during short KV cache rebuilds and autoscaling windows; runbooks are often executed manually leading to cognitive load and delayed mitigations.

High-level approach: implement a middle-layer (alert-dampener) that consumes alerts from the routing tier, enriches with SLO burn rate, modelled service capacity, and recent mitigation actions, and decides to pass, suppress-with-annotation, or auto-trigger a playbook.

Key components: alert-dampener service (stateless front ends + stateful short-memory store for suppression tokens), circuit interlock engine (stores region bond state and global failover policy), runbook executor (safe sandbox for automated steps), and observability surfaces in Console.

Edge cases: suppressions must not mask progressive total-loss events; we will implement a progressive escalation window and out-of-band safety checks that force escalation when correlated signals cross higher thresholds.
Security/ops: all automated remediation steps must be auditable and recorded in an incident timeline; least-privilege service accounts used for runbook actions.
